release_candidate.verification: git status --porcelain=v1 -uno => empty; git log -1 --format="%H %s" => matches 115f698 exactly

scope: Independently re-verify EV-019, EV-020, EV-021 from Swapnil/Kabir's finding set, opening cited code directly in the RC checkout and attempting to refute each (reachability, missing guards, provenance, severity).

questions.q: Does Deliverable.milestoneId ever get populated anywhere in the codebase after a Deliverable row is created?
questions.a: No. The only place Deliverable rows are ever built is ContractService.materializeDeliverables (ContractService.java:764-772) via Deliverable.builder(), and that builder call chain never invokes .milestoneId(...). Deliverable has no setter, only the Builder method. grep across influora-api/src/main confirms zero other call sites that could set it post-creation, and no migration/native UPDATE touches deliverables.milestone_id.

questions.q: Does the approval flow's automatic escrow release depend on Deliverable.milestoneId?
questions.a: Yes. BrandDeliverableService.approve() (line 191) calls escrowService.tryReleaseOnApproval(workspace.getId(), deliverable.getMilestoneId()) directly, and EscrowService.tryReleaseOnApproval (EscrowService.java ~729) returns ReleaseOutcome.held("NO_MILESTONE") whenever that id is null/blank.

questions.q: Is there existing committed test evidence that documents/asserts NO_MILESTONE-for-every-approval?
questions.a: Yes. BrandDeliverableServiceTest.java lines 222-234 carry the exact comment 'Deliverable.milestoneId is never populated (contract generation materializes deliverables without it, by design), so tryReleaseOnApproval answers NO_MILESTONE for EVERY approval', and a test at line ~321 asserts NO_MILESTONE for a normal approval. Ran `mvn -q -o -Dtest=BrandDeliverableServiceTest,ContractServiceTest test`: both green (32/32 and 39/39, 0 failures, 0 errors).

questions.q: Is there an alternative, working path for a brand to manually release escrowed funds without relying on auto-release-on-approval?
questions.a: Yes. POST /wallet/escrow/release (EscrowController.release) accepts either milestoneId or escrowHoldId and is wired to a real UI control in src/components/brand/deal-room/deal-payments-tab.tsx (handleRelease -> api.payments.releasePayout), landed under fix tag F-0224 whose own comment says the endpoint 'existed with ZERO callers anywhere in the app' before this — i.e. this manual-release UI is itself a recent fix for exactly the gap EV-019 describes.

questions.q: Does that manual release path depend on the broken Deliverable.milestoneId link?
questions.a: No. The milestone id it uses comes from GET /contracts/:id's ContractMilestone list (real payment_milestones rows), independent of Deliverable.milestoneId, so it is not blocked by EV-019's defect.

questions.q: Does BrandDeliverableService.approve() enforce any workspace-member role (OWNER/ADMIN) before approving and triggering a release attempt?
questions.a: No. approve() only calls brandContext.requireBrandWorkspace(principal), which checks user-type==BRAND, not soft-deleted, and workspace not suspended — it never calls requireMember or requireRole. requireBrandDeliverable() adds only a workspace-scoped findByIdAndWorkspaceId lookup. No role check exists anywhere in this chain.

questions.q: Does EscrowService.tryReleaseOnApproval itself enforce the brand OWNER/ADMIN role gate that EscrowService.release()/releaseByHoldId() enforce?
questions.a: No — and this is explicit, not accidental. Its own javadoc (EscrowService.java ~707-716) states it runs the same release gates '... but WITHOUT the brand OWNER/ADMIN role gate: the caller has already been authorized for this workspace by BrandContextService#requireBrandWorkspace ... a plain workspace member who can review deliverables must not be blocked from triggering the release their own approval unlocks.'

questions.q: Is there a Spring Security filter-level restriction on /deliverables/** by workspace role?
questions.a: No. SecurityConfig.java only gates by user TYPE (hasRole("ADMIN") for /admin/**, an equivalent matcher for /creator/**); there is no workspace-member-role (OWNER/ADMIN/MEMBER/VIEWER) matcher anywhere, and /deliverables/** falls through to the general authenticated-BRAND-or-CREATOR rule.

questions.q: Is creator self-serve bank withdrawal actually disabled in the deployed configuration, and is that enforced client-side only or also server-side?
questions.a: VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=false is set in both Dockerfile (default ARG, line ~58) and .env.production (line 73) with an explicit comment: 'documented collection live, payouts manual operating state'. This is a Vite build-time variable baked into the frontend bundle only — grep of influora-api/src/main finds zero backend references to any PAYOUTS_ENABLED-style flag. WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal (POST /wallet/withdraw) has no such gate and remains live and reachable server-side regardless of the frontend flag.

questions.q: Does AdminFinanceService.recordManualPayout (the manual-UTR admin payout path) really require SUPER_ADMIN specifically, or does ADMIN also qualify?
questions.a: Confirmed SUPER_ADMIN only: adminContext.requireRoleWithMfaSatisfied(principal, AdminRole.SUPER_ADMIN) at the top of recordManualPayout (line ~160, inside the cited 150-272 range). This is a single-role call, distinct from getEscrowSummary a few lines below it in the same file, which explicitly allows SUPER_ADMIN and ADMIN. So 'every manual payout needs a SUPER_ADMIN' is accurate for this specific action.

questions.q: Does RazorpayXClient.isConfigured() actually distinguish a genuine credential from the literal placeholder values shipped in application.yml defaults and deploy/utho/generate-env.sh?
questions.a: No. RazorpayXClient.isConfigured() (lines 108-110) = props.isConfigured() && !payoutAccountNumber.isBlank(); RazorpayProperties.isConfigured() only checks keyId/keySecret non-null-and-non-blank — no placeholder-value detection. deploy/utho/generate-env.sh literally sets RAZORPAY_KEY_ID=rzp_test_REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY, RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET=REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_RAZORPAY_SECRET, RAZORPAYX_ACCOUNT_NUMBER=REPLACE_ME — all non-blank strings. Given these deployed defaults, isConfigured() evaluates to boolean true even though nothing is actually configured.

questions.q: Is there an existing test that exercises the real deployed placeholder strings (not just the blank-string case) against isConfigured()?
questions.a: No. Ran `mvn -q -o -Dtest=RazorpayXClientTest test`: 11/11 pass, 0 failures. But RazorpayXClientTest.java line 44 states 'Defaults are blank ("")' — it only tests the empty-string case, never the literal REPLACE_ME/REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY placeholder strings that deploy/utho/generate-env.sh actually ships. Genuine test-coverage gap matching this account's own 'tests skip the real production shape' pattern.

questions.q: If a creator calls POST /wallet/withdraw directly while RazorpayX is misconfigured as deployed, does the wallet get debited before the (failing) RazorpayX call?
questions.a: Yes, by the code's own documentation: WalletService.java lines ~201-205 state 'Both doProcessWithdrawal ... and PayoutService#doQueuePayout ... debit Wallet#getBalance() before ever calling RazorpayX'. PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob exists specifically to sweep this exact orphaned-debit class, which corroborates it is a known, real, already-partially-mitigated (by a sweep job, not by prevention) risk rather than a hypothetical one.

questions.q: Are all three findings' cited files/paths actually present and matching in the clean RC commit (not the working tree's uncommitted delta)?
questions.a: Yes for all three. ContractService.java, EscrowService.java, BrandDeliverableService.java, AdminFinanceService.java (at service/admin/AdminFinanceService.java — one directory level different from the finding's cited path but the same file/content), RazorpayXClient.java, Dockerfile and .env.production all exist at the cited (or near-cited) locations inside C:/Users/Sage world/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/rc-115f698, and `git status --porcelain=v1 -uno` in that checkout is empty, confirming a clean 115f698 tree.

questions.q: Does fixing EV-019 (populating milestoneId) make EV-021's authorization gap immediately exploitable for real fund movement?
questions.a: Yes. The disagreement note attached to EV-021 ('the release side is inert today because of EV-019, and becomes live once EV-019 is fixed') is accurate: nothing about a milestoneId-population fix would also add the missing OWNER/ADMIN role check inside tryReleaseOnApproval, so the two findings are independent defects that currently mask each other's blast radius.

verdicts.title: Deliverable approval never releases payment (Deliverable.milestoneId never populated); no auto-release
verdicts.reason: Statically confirmed the only Deliverable-creation path (ContractService.java:764-772, materializeDeliverables) never calls Builder.milestoneId(...), and no other write path in influora-api/src/main sets deliverables.milestone_id. Confirmed EscrowService.tryReleaseOnApproval's real implementation returns ReleaseOutcome.held("NO_MILESTONE") whenever milestoneId is null/blank. Executed `mvn -q -o -Dtest=BrandDeliverableServiceTest,ContractServiceTest test` in the RC: 32/32 and 39/39 tests pass, including a committed test/comment (lines 222-234, ~321-323 of BrandDeliverableServiceTest.java) that explicitly documents and asserts NO_MILESTONE for every approval 'by design'. The core technical claim is not just plausible but is committed, self-documented, and test-covered as an accepted (if under-communicated) production behavior.
verdicts.downgrade_note: Severity nuance the original finding did not surface: the same RC commit already ships a working MITIGATION — a manual 'Release payment' button (F-0224, src/components/brand/deal-room/deal-payments-tab.tsx handleRelease -> POST /wallet/escrow/release with a real ContractMilestone id, independent of the broken Deliverable.milestoneId link) that lets a brand OWNER/ADMIN manually complete the release for any FUNDED milestone. So the money is NOT irrecoverably stuck/refund-only as the 'stays FUNDED and refundable' phrasing implies — it requires an extra manual step the product does not prompt for at approval time. Kept at P1 because the advertised core flow ("approving a deliverable pays the creator") is broken 100% of the time with no in-product prompt pointing the brand at the manual workaround, which is a genuine go-live reliability/UX defect even though it is not a permanent fund-loss defect.
verdicts.new_evidence: Confirmed manual-release mitigation exists in the same RC (F-0224, deal-payments-tab.tsx + EscrowController.release); confirmed via direct execution that the existing test suite documents and green-asserts this exact NO_MILESTONE-for-every-approval behavior 'by design'.

verdicts.title: Creator bank payout not self-serve in prod: withdraw off by default, payouts are manual admin UTR entries
verdicts.reason: Confirmed VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=false in both Dockerfile (default ARG ~line 58) and .env.production (line 73), explicitly documented as the deliberate 'collection live, payouts manual' state. Confirmed this is a frontend-only Vite build flag with zero backend enforcement (grep of influora-api/src/main finds no reference) — WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal (POST /wallet/withdraw) remains live and reachable server-side with no admin/role/feature-flag gate of its own. Confirmed AdminFinanceService.recordManualPayout (line ~160, inside the cited 150-272 range) requires AdminRole.SUPER_ADMIN specifically (single-role check, MFA-satisfied), distinct from the SUPER_ADMIN+ADMIN pair used a few lines below for read-only escrow summary access — so 'every manual payout needs a SUPER_ADMIN' is accurate. Confirmed RazorpayXClient.isConfigured() (lines 108-110) only checks non-blank keyId/keySecret/payoutAccountNumber with no placeholder-value detection, and confirmed deploy/utho/generate-env.sh literally ships RAZORPAY_KEY_ID=rzp_test_REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY, RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET=REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_RAZORPAY_SECRET, RAZORPAYX_ACCOUNT_NUMBER=REPLACE_ME — all non-blank, so isConfigured() deterministically evaluates true against these real deployed defaults, meaning the client would attempt a real (failing) network call rather than gracefully short-circuiting.
verdicts.downgrade_note: Evidence score held at 3 rather than 4 because I did not execute a new runtime check against the literal placeholder strings (the audit's read-only-on-source rule precludes adding a temporary test file to the RC to prove it end-to-end); the existing RazorpayXClientTest (ran 11/11 green) only covers the blank-string case, which IS a genuine test-coverage gap worth flagging on its own, but the isConfigured() boolean logic itself is simple enough (non-blank checks on values I directly confirmed in the deploy script) that confidence is set very high (90) despite the static-only evidence score.
verdicts.new_evidence: Confirmed WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal has no backend-side flag gate at all (VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED is FE-only), so the 'withdraw off by default' protection is UI-only and the backend money-out path is fully live; confirmed the wallet debit happens before the RazorpayX call (WalletService.java ~201-205 javadoc), and that PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob exists specifically to sweep the resulting orphaned-debit class, corroborating this as an already-partially-mitigated-by-cleanup (not prevented) risk.

verdicts.title: Any workspace member (incl. VIEWER) can approve a deliverable; approval is wired to escrow release, bypassing OWNER/ADMIN gate
verdicts.reason: Confirmed the full call chain for BrandDeliverableService.approve() (lines 128-187): it calls only brandContext.requireBrandWorkspace(principal) (checks BRAND user-type, not soft-deleted, workspace not suspended — no membership/role check) and a private requireBrandDeliverable(workspace, id) (a workspace-scoped lookup only). Neither requireMember() nor requireRole() is ever called anywhere in this path. Confirmed EscrowService.tryReleaseOnApproval's own javadoc (~lines 707-716) explicitly states it runs the same release gates as EscrowService.release()/releaseByHoldId() 'but WITHOUT the brand OWNER/ADMIN role gate', calling this deliberate. Confirmed SecurityConfig.java has no workspace-role-based filter matcher for /deliverables/** (only user-TYPE matchers for /admin/** and /creator/**). Confirmed the frontend deliverable-review-panel.tsx has no role/VIEWER/OWNER/ADMIN gating either, so there is no defense at any layer. Ran the existing BrandDeliverableServiceTest suite (32/32 green); it contains no negative test for a VIEWER-role principal being rejected, consistent with (not contradicting) the absence of the claimed gate.
verdicts.downgrade_note: None material — this is a genuine, reachable, multi-layer-confirmed authorization gap. The one caveat (already captured correctly in the original finding's own 'disagreement' field) is that the release side-effect of an unauthorized approval is currently inert because of EV-019 (Deliverable.milestoneId is never populated, so tryReleaseOnApproval always answers NO_MILESTONE regardless of who called approve()) — but the authorization defect itself is live today for the deliverable-status-change/collaboration-lifecycle side effects of approve(), and would immediately become a live fund-release bypass the moment EV-019 is fixed without EV-021 also being fixed.
verdicts.new_evidence: Confirmed absence of any role gate at three independent layers (Spring Security filter config, BrandContextService, and the FE review panel component), and confirmed via the service's own javadoc that the missing gate in tryReleaseOnApproval is an intentional design choice, not an oversight — which if anything strengthens rather than weakens the finding, since it shows the gap was reasoned about but the workspace-role dimension was never closed.
